decisions.reason: The evening psychiatric day-patient program has its own page and required substantial staffing and licensing investment, and it fits the firm's psychiatric care direction, so management will attribute weak uptake to start-up effects and keep it.

The carpentry workshop is publicly presented on its own page and has sunk costs in equipment, and it serves the firm's inclusion mission, so management will persist despite being further from core care.
Outpatient sociotherapy is only mentioned and carries little public commitment, but it is cheap to run, reimbursed by health insurers and closely tied to psychiatric care, so dropping it is unlikely.
Senior living counseling is shown on the home page and signals the firm's announced strategic direction, so the strong public commitment and need for justification make continuation very likely.

The retail shop is only mentioned on the website and is the most peripheral of the products, which makes it the likeliest to be dropped, but its link to the sheltered workshop and its modest costs still favor keeping it.
